summary: The deterministic routing core is promising, but the implementation currently exposes false mutation authorization, ignores the documented environment kill switch, accepts stale or path-escaping inputs, emits unusable rule identifiers, and has incomplete privacy and schema validation. These issues should block release.

findings.claim: Every router decision claims mutation is allowed even though this wave implements no mutation gate or required-rule receipt verification.
findings.analysis: The host-facing `enforcement` field is derived only from semantic-provider status. It is unrelated to whether concern-required rules were loaded, acknowledged, hash-verified, or executed. In the normal unavailable-semantic path, the router returns `mutation-allowed-degraded`; a future adapter consuming the normalized contract could therefore authorize mutation despite the plan explicitly deferring enforcement to Wave 5.
evidence: scripts/lib/skill-router.mjs sets `enforcement: semanticStatus === "active" ? "mutation-allowed" : "mutation-allowed-degraded"`.
The same module only lists concern matches; it performs no content-hash receipt or executable-twin verification.
The manifest states that mutation-gate rollout is deferred to Wave 5 while describing this result as host-facing.
findings.proposed_fix: Until Wave 5 exists, return a non-authorizing state such as `advisory-only` or `read-only-diagnosis`, add it to the schema, and require positive rule-receipt/check evidence before any `mutation-allowed` result.

findings.claim: The documented `SVC_SKILL_ROUTER_MODE` safety and rollback control has no effect.
findings.analysis: The CLI never reads `SVC_SKILL_ROUTER_MODE`; absent `--mode`, it always selects `suggest`. Thus setting the advertised kill switch to `off` still runs discovery and writes receipts. The implementation also throws for an unknown value rather than applying the manifest's documented fail-closed-to-off behavior.
evidence: scripts/skill-router.mjs passes `mode: args.mode || "suggest"`.
No router file reads `process.env.SVC_SKILL_ROUTER_MODE`.
The manifest's External State section says the library reads this variable on each invocation and unknown values fail closed to off.
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve mode as explicit flag, then `SVC_SKILL_ROUTER_MODE`, then the documented default. Convert invalid environment values to `off` with a diagnostic, and add tests proving `off` suppresses optional discovery and receipt emission.

findings.claim: Runtime routing accepts stale or tampered compiled indexes without checking their canonical-input or skill-content hashes.
findings.analysis: The compiler records manifest, overrides, concern-registry, and per-skill hashes, but `loadIndex` validates only `schema_version`. It even calculates the artifact hash and never uses it. Routing can consequently combine a stale index with the current concern registry, violating the content-addressed and deterministic-input contract. The promised exact-only degraded fallback on a hash mismatch is absent.
evidence: scripts/lib/skill-router.mjs `loadIndex` checks only `index.schema_version !== 1`.
`compiled_from.*_sha256` and each record's `content_hash` are never verified at route time.
The returned `artifactHash` is unused.
plan-contract.json promises hash-mismatch detection and exact-name-only fallback.
findings.proposed_fix: Verify all canonical-input hashes before ranked routing and validate selected skill content hashes before load. On mismatch, disable lexical/alias routing, retain only safely re-derived exact resolution, record a stale-index diagnostic, and add stale-index fixtures.

findings.claim: A malicious skill name can escape the repository during compilation and read an arbitrary `SKILL.md` path.
findings.analysis: Manifest skill names are joined directly into a filesystem path without enforcing the schema's kebab-case constraint or checking realpath containment. A value containing `..` can escape `root/skills`. The generated schema does not prevent this because the compiler never validates against it, and its path regex also permits traversal segments.
evidence: scripts/compile-skill-router-index.mjs constructs `path.join(root, "skills", name, "SKILL.md")` from unvalidated manifest data.
No compiler check enforces `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`.
schemas/skill-routing-index.schema.json uses `^skills/.+/SKILL\\.md$`, which accepts `skills/../../.../SKILL.md`.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate every included skill name before path construction, reject separators and traversal segments, canonicalize the resolved file, and require it to remain beneath the canonical `root/skills/<name>` directory. Add traversal and symlink-escape negative tests.

findings.claim: Concern-required rules are returned as decorated prose rather than loadable rule identifiers.
findings.analysis: The normalized `rules` contract describes an array of rule IDs, but `resolvePins` appends concern evidence to each ID. Consumers cannot reliably resolve a value such as `security-boundary (concern:auth-surface)` to the registered rule, and duplicate rules are not deduplicated. This breaks the deterministic critical-rule handoff even before mutation enforcement is introduced.
evidence: scripts/lib/skill-router.mjs pushes ``${r} (concern:${concern.name})`` into `rules`.
schemas/skill-router-decision.schema.json describes `rules` as required rule identifiers.
Pin evidence already has a separate structured `pins_evidence` channel.
findings.proposed_fix: Return exact, deduplicated rule IDs in `rules`; record concern and signal evidence in a separate structured rule-evidence field. Test exact equality against known registry IDs.

findings.claim: Alias collision validation misses aliases that collide with another skill's canonical name.
findings.analysis: The alias-owner map is populated only from aliases. An override may therefore give skill A an alias equal to canonical skill B. An exact request then pins both records rather than failing compilation, contrary to the global-owner and pin-conflict contracts.
evidence: scripts/compile-skill-router-index.mjs initializes `aliasOwners` empty and never seeds it with `includedSkills`.
scripts/lib/skill-router.mjs independently matches each record's canonical name and aliases and accumulates all matches.
The corpus tests alias-to-alias behavior only indirectly and has no canonical-name collision fixture.
findings.proposed_fix: Seed the normalized owner map with every canonical name, reject alias-to-canonical and duplicate-within-entry collisions, and add a fixture proving compilation fails with the named owners.

findings.claim: Privacy-safe receipts can contain raw caller-supplied file paths.
findings.analysis: Concern pin evidence embeds the complete matching path and the entire decision is appended to the receipt stream. CLI `--files` values are caller-controlled and may contain customer names, secret-bearing filenames, or other sensitive text. The redaction test examines only raw intent and therefore misses this leak.
evidence: matchConcern returns `path:${hitPath}`.
resolvePins includes that value in `receipt.pins_evidence[].evidence`.
writeReceipt appends the complete decision object.
validate-skill-router.sh seeds only `--intent` for its redaction check and supplies no sensitive file path.
findings.proposed_fix: Store a stable signal ID plus a truncated path fingerprint or sanitized repository-relative category, not the raw path. Extend redaction tests with secret-bearing file, environment, package, and concern evidence.

findings.claim: The claimed JSON Schema conformance is not actually tested or enforced.
findings.analysis: `validateDecision` is a partial handwritten checker and assumes nested fields exist; it does not enforce most enums, required nested properties, additional-property restrictions, timestamps, item shapes, or rule/string types. The index schema is likewise never applied. The validator can therefore report schema conformance while substantial contract violations pass.
evidence: validateDecision checks a small subset of schemas/skill-router-decision.schema.json and directly accesses `decision.suggestions.length` and `decision.budget.*`.
scripts/skill-router.mjs `validate` checks only descriptions and policy counts.
validate-skill-router.sh calls only the handwritten validator; no Draft 2020-12 validator or equivalent exhaustive checks appear.
findings.proposed_fix: Use a real Draft 2020-12 validator or a repository-local exhaustive schema checker for both artifacts and decisions. Add mutation tests for every required field, enum, additional property, and nested item shape.

findings.claim: Adding the active-mode ambiguity fallback makes recorded D1 budget counters inaccurate.
findings.analysis: D1 tokens and card count are computed before `route-workflow` is unshifted. After fallback insertion, the receipt can report zero tokens for one emitted card or nine cards while only eight suggestions are serialized. This violates the plan's requirement to count injected tokens and makes budget telemetry unreliable.
evidence: scripts/lib/skill-router.mjs calculates `d1Tokens` during the initial budget loop.
The active-mode fallback later calls `cards.unshift(...)`.
`budget.d1_cards` uses `cards.length`, while `suggestions` uses `cards.slice(0, 8)` and no fallback token cost is added.
The ambiguity corpus checks only the head suggestion, not counter consistency.
findings.proposed_fix: Insert the fallback before the final budget cut or recompute tokens, card count, and truncation after insertion. Assert that counters exactly equal the serialized suggestion set.

findings.claim: The research log contains an accidental diff-header artifact.
findings.analysis: A literal `++ b/docs/specs/research-log.md` line appears to have been inserted at the start of the new research entry, degrading the durable documentation artifact.
evidence: The research-log hunk adds a line rendered as `+++ b/docs/specs/research-log.md` inside the hunk immediately before the new heading.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove the stray `++ b/docs/specs/research-log.md` content line and verify the rendered Markdown.
